statements.text: I'm not somebody who believes that the AI is just a total bubble or that there's nothing happening here. [...] Obviously, it is very capable and getting more so every day.
statements.venue: Vox Today, Explained podcast, 'The AI election'

statements.text: Right now, there's no regulation at all that is protecting people. [...] That's why we need a federal moratorium on new data centers, so that we can all have a society-wide dialogue about what are the appropriate regulations to ensure that if these data centers are built, it is for the benefit of all of our people, rather than just a few billionaires in Silicon Valley.
I signed the AI Pact because Michiganders shouldn’t have to pay the price for a technology built to enrich Silicon Valley billionaires and the politicians cashing the checks
statements.venue: Statement on signing the AI Pact, Gander Newsroom

statements.text: AI development is out of control. Tech billionaires are bulldozing towns and farms to build data centers to make themselves even richer. They’re threatening Michigan jobs, driving up our energy costs, and contaminating our air and water.
statements.venue: Campaign Stop Tech Overreach (STOP) plan PDF

statements.text: All across this district, everyday Michiganders are standing up and fighting back against the Big Tech companies trying to bulldoze their communities. These companies are trying to force their way into our towns to build a mass unemployment machine that no one wants and that AI experts worry could wipe out all of humanity. I am proud to stand shoulder to shoulder with my neighbors and fight for Mid-Michigan.
statements.venue: News release quoted by Michigan Public on the Stop Tech Overreach plan

statements.text: We need to put a stop to this, because right now the whole thing is out of control and alarm bells are going off,
statements.venue: Press conference in Mason, MI, as quoted by CBS Detroit

statements.text: If I had to choose, I’d say data centers because that’s where people in the district are finding some common ground across the spectrum — in fighting back against the concentrated power in Silicon Valley, which has been fully enabled by [incumbent Rep.] Tom Barrett and Donald Trump.

Communities should have the final say over whether a data center comes to town and how the benefits are shared. That is why I released a comprehensive plan to stop tech overreach. It calls for Congress to pause data center construction and advanced AI development, then pass a national AI compact that protects workers, water, and our energy bills.
statements.venue: Candidate Q&A on the issues, Argus-Press
